hero.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls to Lowest Level Since May as US–Iran Conflict Escalates
hero.description: The US–Iran confrontation continues to shake global energy markets as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz falls sharply. Nigeria's Dangote Refinery IPO, a remarkable survivor rescue in Nepal and severe flooding in China are also among the major stories this morning.

featured.title: Hormuz Shipping Disruption Deepens as US–Iran Conflict Keeps Oil Markets on Edge
featured.content: The Strait of Hormuz is becoming an increasingly important pressure point in the US–Iran conflict. Reuters reports that an average of only about 10 commodity ships per day crossed the waterway during the past 10 days, the lowest traffic level since May. The decline is raising fresh concerns about global oil supplies, shipping costs and inflation.

articles.title: Hormuz shipping traffic falls to lowest level since May
articles.content: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply following recent attacks involving US and Iranian forces. Reuters reports that an average of around 10 commodity ships per day crossed the waterway during the past 10 days, the lowest level since May. The Strait is one of the world's most important energy shipping routes.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz oil tanker traffic

articles.title: US–Iran confrontation continues around vessels
articles.content: US and Iranian forces exchanged fire around vessels near Iran over the weekend. The United States said it struck three Iranian oil carriers, while Iran said it targeted vessels it considered to be using unauthorised routes. The confrontation is adding to concerns about the safety of commercial shipping and global energy supplies.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran conflict oil tanker Strait of Hormuz

articles.title: Oil markets remain under pressure from Hormuz disruption
articles.content: Crude prices ended last week substantially higher after renewed US–Iran strikes. Investors are now closely watching shipping activity through Hormuz because prolonged disruption could increase the cost of transporting oil and other commodities around the world.
articles.imageQuery: global oil market crude oil barrels

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO approved by Nigeria's SEC
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the planned Dangote Refinery IPO. The proposed offering involves 4.1 billion shares priced at ₦525 each and could raise approximately ₦2.15 trillion, or about $1.63 billion. The refinery currently has a capacity of 650,000 barrels per day and Dangote plans to expand it towards 1.4 million barrels per day. The order book is expected to open on September 14.

articles.title: Nigeria pipeline incident reportedly leaves at least 37 dead
articles.content: An environmental group says at least 37 people died after inhaling fumes while attempting to tap an oil pipeline in southern Nigeria. Nigerian authorities had not independently confirmed the reported death toll in the Reuters report. RadiantWaves therefore presents the 37 figure as a reported claim rather than an official confirmed toll.

articles.title: Nigeria could double energy investment within five years
articles.content: International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol says Nigeria could potentially double investment in its energy sector within five years. He pointed to opportunities across oil, gas and renewable energy as Nigeria strengthens its relationship with the IEA.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria oil gas renewable energy investment

articles.title: Nigeria's economy records stronger second-quarter growth
articles.content: Nigeria's economy grew 4.43% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, up from 3.89% in the first quarter, according to official data reported by Reuters. Growth was supported by both oil and non-oil sectors.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria economy Lagos business financial market

articles.title: Nepali woman rescued alive after 10 days underground
articles.content: Chandika Kumari Shrestha, an elderly Nepali woman, was found alive 10 days after her family had begun mourning her presumed death. Rescuers discovered her trapped inside an air pocket in the remains of her collapsed four-storey home in Betrawati. She was taken to an army hospital after the rescue.

articles.title: Nepal disaster leaves more than 1,300 dead
articles.content: The devastating disaster along the Nepal–Tibet border has killed more than 1,300 people, while nearly 5,000 remain missing according to the latest Reuters reporting. Rescue teams continue searching through mud, concrete and debris for possible survivors.

articles.title: Another survivor rescued from Nepal hydropower tunnel
articles.content: A Chinese national was rescued alive from a tunnel at Nepal's Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project after spending 10 days underground. He became the third person rescued alive from tunnels in the affected area. Rescue teams continue searching for others who may still be trapped.

articles.title: Typhoon Saudel brings severe flooding to southern China
articles.content: Typhoon Saudel has brought torrential rain and flooding to southern China's coastal provinces, particularly Fujian and Guangdong. More than 83,000 people were evacuated in Fujian, while schools and transport services were disrupted. Authorities remain alert for further flooding and landslides.

articles.title: Dover traffic disrupted by masked protests
articles.content: Groups of masked protesters disrupted roads around Dover, one of Britain's main ferry gateways to France. The demonstrations caused traffic disruption around the port as migration remains a highly sensitive political issue in Britain.
articles.imageQuery: Dover port protest UK ferry France

articles.title: Russia keeps possible Trump–Putin–Xi meeting on the table
articles.content: Russia says it has not ruled out a possible trilateral meeting involving Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Discussions could potentially take place around the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November, although no meeting has been agreed.
articles.imageQuery: Trump Putin Xi Jinping diplomatic meeting

articles.title: Global markets monitor geopolitical and energy risks
articles.content: Investors are watching oil prices, shipping costs and inflation expectations closely as the US–Iran confrontation affects energy markets. Central-bank policy and the wider global economy remain additional areas of focus.

articles.title: US economy faces fresh energy-price pressures
articles.content: American consumers and businesses are facing renewed uncertainty over fuel and transportation costs as Middle East tensions push crude prices higher. Any prolonged disruption around Hormuz could increase pressure on inflation and household budgets.

morningSummary: Good morning. Monday begins with the Strait of Hormuz at the centre of global attention as shipping traffic falls to its lowest level since May amid continuing US–Iran tensions. Nigeria has major economic and energy developments, while Nepal has produced another extraordinary survivor story amid a devastating disaster. Severe flooding continues in China, and Dover traffic has been disrupted by protests.
bigQuestion: With conflicts increasingly affecting energy, shipping and the global economy, how can governments protect ordinary citizens from the economic consequences of geopolitical crises?
